this_round_summary: User instruction: '보류한 것도 마저 해!!! 다만 불가능한건 어쩔수없고' (finish what was deferred too, except what's genuinely impossible). The two items the prior round (e577107/434120c) had deliberately left as low-priority (zero live callers meant zero behavioral risk today) were closed: (1) etl/kg.py's party-name merge grouped only by normalized(name), not (scope, normalized) -- a bond issuer and a domestic-ETP manager that normalize to the same string (normalize_party treats Ltd/LLC/Inc/㈜/주식회사 as interchangeable suffixes) would collapse into one KG party node despite being different real-world entities in different product scopes. Fixed: groupby now includes scope, node_id changed from party:<normalized> to party:<scope>:<normalized>, with edge dst_node_id and alias node_id updated to match. Rebuilding the real database against the fix changed the actual counts (+12 nodes, +17 aliases) -- confirming this was a real, not just theoretical, data-correctness bug: 12 genuine cross-scope name collisions existed in the live 60,903-product dataset. (2) etl/kg.py had zero dedicated tests for its own role-assignment/merge/alias-kind logic (only coarse structural invariants). Added tests/unit/test_kg.py, 8 tests, in-memory synthetic DuckDB (same style as test_lexical.py) -- including a direct regression test for the scope-collision fix. Writing that test caught a second, real bug before it could ever bite: a synthetic fixture with zero bond/ETP rows left the intermediate parties frame empty, and DuckDB mis-inferred kg_edge's edge_id column as INT32 from that empty CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, breaking on the next real-string INSERT. Cannot happen against the actual 145K-row source (bonds/ETPs are never universally absent an issuer/manager), but cheap to guard against with explicit CAST(...AS VARCHAR); fixed. Full re-verification after both fixes and a real database rebuild: pytest 246/246, eval 640/640 (100%, unchanged as expected since this path isn't live yet), metamorphic 137/137, ruff clean, compliance 84/0. No deferred items remain from either review round.
